archetype.name: Play-In Team (sputtering start)
archetype.definition: A Clippers group whose shooting and recent history point to the middle of the West, but whose turnovers and soft interior defense have it playing like a lottery team six games in.

report.headline: Good shooting, bad possessions: a 1-5 start built on giveaways and a leaky rim
report.take:
The Clippers are 1-5 and 27th on the site, and the margin backs up the record. A -7.4 Net Rtg ranks 22nd, the point differential implies only two wins, and they have lost five straight by an average of 13.8. This is not a team being robbed in close games. After a 121-96 opening win over Sacramento, every game has been a clear loss, including two to the Lakers.

The odd part is that the shooting is fine. Their 38.6 3P% ranks 5th and TS % sits right at league average, in line with a franchise that has hit 36.8 to 38.1 percent from three every recent season. The offense ranks 25th in ORtg at 107.4 anyway because it keeps throwing the ball away. The 18.4 TOV % is dead last, 4.3 above the league, and no recent Clippers team was above 13.4. The ball runs through Darius Garland, whose 31 USG % comes with a -4.4 BPM and a -27 On-Off. Kris Dunn has a 4.2 BPM and +17.5 On-Off on 11.9 usage. Rui Hachimura's 47.7 TS % and -20.1 On-Off make the frontcourt D look generous.

The defense is the second leak. Opponents shoot 57 eFG % (28th) and 71.8% at the rim (27th), and they get there more than against almost anyone. Shooting guards have carried 41.7% of the scoring against the Clippers, against a league norm near a quarter, and post 47.5 points a game, 7 over their usual output. At small forward, the one spot where a B wing group lives, opponents are held to the fewest points in the league. The defense is getting beaten at the point of attack and in the paint, not on the wings.

Six games is a thin sample, and some of this should ease. A turnover rate this far outside the franchise's history usually comes back toward normal, and rim percentages this extreme rarely hold. But the roster grades (D backcourt, D frontcourt) don't describe a 50-win team either. The realistic ceiling is the low-to-mid play-in range, and getting there starts with fewer giveaways and less of Hachimura's inefficiency.

strengths.title: The jump shot is real
strengths.body: A 38.6 3P% ranks 5th, 3.9 points above the league, at an average share of threes. Every recent Clippers team shot well from deep, so this looks like a skill rather than a hot week. Derrick Jones Jr. (66.8 TS %) and Brook Lopez (64.1) are giving efficient volume around it.

strengths.title: Dunn and the wings hold up
strengths.body: Kris Dunn is the team's best player by the numbers: 4.2 BPM, 64.7 TS %, +17.5 On-Off and 12th on the PG tab. The wing group grades B, and opposing small forwards score less against the Clippers than against anyone in the league. The perimeter defense also forces turnovers at a top-six rate, which gives the team a base to build lineups around.

concerns.title: Worst turnover rate in the league
concerns.body: At 18.4, the TOV % ranks 30th and sits 4.3 above the league average. It is the main reason an offense with above-average shooting efficiency ranks 25th in ORtg. It is also far outside this franchise's norm (13.2 last season), so it should improve. Until it does, Garland's -27 On-Off on 31% usage is the number that defines the offense.

concerns.title: No resistance at the rim
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 71.8% within four feet, 6.5 above the league, and take an above-average share of their shots there. Shooting guards are scoring 47.5 a game against this defense. That points to guards getting downhill with nobody behind them. Part of it is small-sample noise, but a D frontcourt grade suggests the problem won't vanish.

concerns.title: Hachimura's start is sinking lineups
concerns.body: A 47.7 TS % on 23.1 usage, a -7.2 BPM and a -20.1 On-Off add up to the roughest line in the rotation. He ranks 67th of 85 on the PF tab. A shooter of his profile likely climbs, but he is costing real possessions for now.

trend.note: An opening blowout win gave way to five straight losses, with the last five games running 6.47 points a game worse than the season margin. Points allowed climbed to 124 in the November loss at Golden State.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games: one stiff test, two real chances
weekAhead.body:
All three games are at home, and the schedule eases after the opener. Toronto is the problem: an 11th-ranked team with a 5th-ranked defense and the league's best rate of forced turnovers. That is the worst possible matchup for an offense that leads the league in giveaways, and the Raptors' elite offensive rebounding adds to it.

Miami and New Orleans are both 2-4, and both have holes the Clippers can use. Miami ranks 24th in DRtg and lets opponents hit 40.5% from three, which suits the league's 5th-best shooting team. New Orleans has been hammered by centers. Its own A- frontcourt and top-five free-throw rate, though, will test a Clippers rim defense that ranks 27th. A 2-1 week is reachable. Anything less deepens the hole.

keyMatchups.title: Clippers giveaways vs. Toronto's pressure
keyMatchups.body: Toronto forces turnovers at the league's highest rate, and the Clippers commit them at the league's highest rate. If the ball security doesn't improve here, the shooting edge won't matter.

keyMatchups.title: Threes against Miami's leaky perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows a 40.5 Opp 3P%, 29th in the league, and gives shooting guards 4.3 points over their norm. That opens the door for Kobe Sanders and Keaton Wagler to give the offense a lift.

keyMatchups.title: Lopez and Jackson vs. New Orleans' centers
keyMatchups.body: Centers score more against the Pelicans than against any other defense, 6.37 points above their usual. Brook Lopez's efficient touches should be a priority. At the other end, the Pelicans' A- frontcourt will attack a Clippers rim defense that has been among the league's softest.

weekAhead.watch: The TOV % against Toronto: if the Clippers can hold up against the league's best ball-hawking defense, the slow start starts to look like noise.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 14 wins and a -601 differential overstates the damage. Two of the worst numbers, a last-place turnover rate and a 71.8% opponent rim percentage, sit far outside anything in this franchise's recent history and should move toward normal. The three-point shooting fits the team's long record, so it should mostly hold. That alone pulls the offense up from 25th toward the middle. I'd expect a Net Rtg somewhere between -4.5 and -0.5 from here, and a final total of 29 to 37 wins.

What probably doesn't regress is the roster shape. D grades in the backcourt and frontcourt, a primary creator with a -4.4 BPM, and thin rim protection make this a team that will need its shooting every night. The defense sat 18th or worse in three of the last four seasons, so a jump into the top ten isn't the base case. Climbing back toward the play-in is plausible. A top-six seed would take Garland and Hachimura playing far better than they have.
swingFactors: Whether the TOV % falls back toward the team's usual 13-14 range
Rim protection from Lopez and Isaiah Jackson

confidence.note: Six games; the turnover and rim numbers are extreme enough to carry heavy small-sample noise.
